solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Meat for Olympic runners-up?

definitions.meaning: a cut of beef from the outer part of the topside, used for roasting or salting
a team that takes second place wins silver medals, so it is the silver team

explanation.surface: A joke about what cut of beef the second-placed Olympic team might be served.
explanation.definitionFit: The beef cut and a team (a side) winning silver both fit the same two words.

clue.text: Supermarket chain mixing Brie and meat

parts.note: Spar is a chain of convenience stores and supermarkets

indicators.note: mixing stirs the letters of the cheese into a new order

explanation.surface: A shop blends cheese and meat into one product.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixing' is the anagram signal on the cheese. Spar is a grocery chain common in Britain and Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut of pork ribs with most of the meat trimmed off is a kind of meat.

clue.text: Turner's leading reprint — 'Foam'

parts.note: a lathe is a machine for turning wood or metal, so it is a turner; the 's stands for 'has'

indicators.note: leading picks the front letter of the word reprint

explanation.surface: Reads as a note about the main reproduction of a Turner painting titled 'Foam'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' suggests the painter J. M. W. Turner, but it is the machine. 'leading' gives R from 'reprint'.
explanation.definitionFit: Soapy froth worked up on skin or a horse's sweat is a synonym of foam.

clue.text: Romeo wandering, holding cross on heathland

indicators.note: holding means the jumbled name keeps the cross inside it
wandering sends the letters of Romeo off in a new order

parts.note: X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: Romeo roams the moors carrying a cross.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering' turns ROMEO into EMOOR; 'holding' puts X after its first letter. Exmoor is a national park of open moorland in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Somerset and Devon moor is a named stretch of open heath and upland.

clue.text: Council and shrine demolished

indicators.note: a building demolished is knocked down, so these letters are rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: A local authority has a religious building pulled down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demolished' rearranges the nine letters of AND SHRINE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sanhedrin was the supreme Jewish court and assembly in ancient Jerusalem, a ruling council.

clue.text: The genie ruffled the majority?

definitions.note: the age of majority, when one legally becomes an adult, is this many years in the UK

indicators.note: ruffled hair or feathers are disordered, so these letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: The genie is upset by most of the people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruffled' rearranges THE GENIE. 'majority' looks like 'most people', but it is the legal coming of age; the question mark flags this example.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming of age in Britain happens at this birthday, so the number stands for legal adulthood.

clue.text: Temporary settlement for half the operations

indicators.note: half signals taking only the front four letters of the eight-letter word for operations

parts.note: a campaign is a series of military operations

explanation.surface: A short-term base is set up to support half of the military's operations.
explanation.definitionFit: Tents or huts put up for a short stay make a provisional settlement.

clue.text: Abridged cantankerous note

indicators.note: abridged means shortened, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: crotchety means irritable and bad-tempered

explanation.surface: A grumpy message has been cut down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' looks like a written message but is the musical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarter note, lasting one beat in common time, is a musical note.

clue.text: Stag party cut connection for instrument

parts.note: a stag party is for men only, so stag suggests a man
a do is a party or celebration

indicators.note: cut docks the last letter of the word

parts.note: a link is a connection

explanation.surface: A bachelor party has its link severed over a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' removes the K from LINK. A stag party is the British name for a bachelor party.
explanation.definitionFit: A lute-like stringed instrument with paired strings, played with a plectrum.

clue.text: Athenian appearing in some element

indicators.note: appearing in places the Athenian inside the word for some

parts.note: any can mean some, as in 'have you any money?'
Timon of Athens is the title character of Shakespeare's play

explanation.surface: An Athenian turns up in some chemical element.
explanation.walkthrough: TIMON goes between A and NY.
explanation.definitionFit: A brittle metalloid with the symbol Sb is a chemical element.

clue.text: Sufficient reason to turn nothing off

indicators.note: off signals that the nothing letter is taken away

parts.note: to go round is to turn
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Reads as a call for a good reason to switch something off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' removes one O from GO ROUND.
explanation.definitionFit: A basis or justification for an action, as in grounds for divorce.

clue.text: Sights to look around, taking in ruins of timeless Troyes

indicators.note: taking in places the jumbled city letters inside
around turns the word for look so it reads the other way

parts.note: to see is to look

indicators.note: ruins of signals the remaining letters are wrecked into a new order
timeless removes T, the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A tourist goes to look around the sights and ruins of the French city of Troyes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'timeless' drops T (time); 'ruins of' rearranges what is left into YESOR; 'around' turns the word for look backwards to EES; 'taking in' puts YESOR inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Ugly structures are sights in the slang sense: things dreadful to look at.

clue.text: Like a tailless rabbit back in US city

indicators.note: back means the phrase is read from end to start

parts.note: a tailless creature has no tail, giving NO
a rabbit's short fluffy tail is its scut, the part it lacks here

explanation.surface: A tailless rabbit is found back in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: A rabbit with no tail has 'no scut' (scut is a rabbit's tail); 'back' turns the whole phrase round.
explanation.definitionFit: The city in southern Arizona is an American city.

clue.text: General removed tip of lath from carbine

indicators.note: removed means the picked letter is taken out of the gun

parts.note: a carbine is a light rifle

indicators.note: tip of picks the first letter of the word lath

explanation.surface: An army general strips the end off a strip of wood from his carbine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General' looks like an army officer but is an adjective. 'tip of' gives L, which 'removed' takes from RIFLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Widespread, as in disease being rife, means general or prevalent.

clue.text: Homestead fitted with one genuine siren

indicators.note: fitted with means the farm has the other pieces installed inside it

parts.note: a homestead is a farm with its house
I is the Roman numeral for one
real means genuine

explanation.surface: A farmhouse has a real siren installed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fitted with' splits the farm after its first letter to take in the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A warning device that sounds a loud alarm when smoke is detected is a kind of siren.

clue.text: Tar over jumper requiring spirit

indicators.note: over means the word for sailor is turned round

parts.note: a tar is a sailor, also AB, able seaman
a cardi, short for cardigan, is a knitted jumper

explanation.surface: Tar spilt on a jumper calls for a stiff drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tar' is the sailor, not the black stuff. A jumper is the British word for a sweater.
explanation.definitionFit: A brand of white rum, so a spirit.

clue.text: Toughened choirboy in Queen's train

indicators.note: in begins the phrase saying where the choirboy goes
following in someone's train means coming behind them, so the choirboy comes after the queen

parts.note: Anne was queen of Great Britain from 1702 to 1714
Aled Jones is a Welsh singer famous as a boy treble

explanation.surface: A tough choirboy follows in the Queen's procession.
explanation.walkthrough: Aled Jones was a famous Welsh choirboy of the 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal or glass heated and slowly cooled is made tougher and less brittle.

clue.text: A fish repeatedly found in jelly

indicators.note: repeatedly means the letter and fish are written twice

parts.note: a gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: A fish turns up again and again in jelly.
explanation.definitionFit: A gelatinous substance from seaweed used to set foods and grow cultures is a jelly.

clue.text: Go canvassing in half of Sandwich

definitions.meaning: to call at people's front doors seeking votes or sales
a very thick slice of bread, such as forms one side of a sandwich

explanation.surface: Someone goes campaigning in part of the Kent town of Sandwich.
explanation.walkthrough: Sandwich is a town in Kent; the capital S hides the food.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the verb for door-to-door canvassing and a chunky bread slice share this word.

clue.text: Pre-prepared for this month

definitions.meaning: ... coffee or food is ready-made, needing only water
in old business letters 'inst.' means of the current month

explanation.surface: Reads as a note that something has been made in advance for the current month.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready-made foods and the old commercial term for the current month share one word.

clue.text: Dancers cut short, holding wife first

indicators.note: holding means the shortened word keeps the other pieces inside
cut docks the last letter of the word

parts.note: terse means short or curt
1st, read as IST, is first

explanation.surface: Dancers have a routine cut short while holding the wife first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' drops the final E, leaving TERS; 'holding' places the wife and first inside, after its T. 'first' reads as 1ST.
explanation.definitionFit: People dancing the Twist, the 1960s craze, are dancers.

clue.text: No-hoper's heading off to expert

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is taken away

parts.note: a goner is someone with no hope of survival

explanation.surface: A no-hoper's boss goes off to see a specialist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading' looks like a noun, but with 'off' it removes the G.
explanation.definitionFit: A oner is British slang for someone or something unique or expert at a thing.

clue.text: Transfer TV duo — yes!

parts.note: Ant and Dec are a British television presenting duo; Dec is one half
Ant is the other half of the presenting pair

explanation.surface: An excited fan cheers a transfer involving a famous TV double act.
explanation.walkthrough: Ant and Dec (Anthony McPartlin and Declan Donnelly) present popular British shows; here the names come in the other order.
explanation.definitionFit: To pour wine from one vessel into another is to transfer it.

clue.text: Garbo chewed either end of expensive herb

indicators.note: chewed means the letters of the name are mangled
either end of picks one of the two outer letters of expensive, both being E

explanation.surface: Greta Garbo chews a pricey herb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chewed' rearranges GARBO into BORAG.
explanation.definitionFit: A blue-flowered plant used in salads and drinks is a herb.

clue.text: Rogue will get fabric cut with gold

indicators.note: cut docks the last letter of the cloth's name

parts.note: terry is a looped towelling fabric
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A rogue gets cloth sliced through with gold thread.
explanation.definitionFit: A little terror is a mischievous child, a rogue or rascal.

clue.text: Anaemic youngsters' cloaks

parts.note: an anaemic person looks pale
tots are small children

explanation.surface: Cloaks belonging to sickly children.
explanation.definitionFit: A paletot is a loose overcoat or cloak.

clue.text: Ruin bishop's day

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
light is daylight, day as opposed to night

explanation.surface: Something has spoilt a bishop's day.
explanation.definitionFit: To blight something is to spoil or wreck it.

clue.text: A little contrary with corrupt files

indicators.note: contrary means the phrase runs the opposite way

parts.note: a tad is a little bit
base means morally low or corrupt

explanation.surface: Reads as a complaint about a few awkward people with crooked records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contrary' turns A TAD into DATA.
explanation.definitionFit: A structured store of records held on a computer is a collection of files.

clue.text: Flower

parts.note: read as flow-er, something that flows, a river

explanation.definitionFit: A river is a thing that flows, and this central European river is one.

clue.text: He was bound for opera house — he's from America

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
the Met is the Metropolitan Opera House in New York
he is taken as written; the 's is 'is'
US is the United States of America

explanation.surface: A man heads for an opera house, being American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound for' looks like 'heading to', but 'bound' belongs with 'He was': the Titan chained to a rock.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Titan who stole fire was chained to a rock as punishment.
